summary: Hold this as a scored submit; the cause is the budget, not the idea. The mechanism is plausible and rules-clean, but the best case is about +0.2% on a headline whose CI is about +/-1.5%. In roughly 60% of outcomes the gate keeps cap 0 everywhere, so the run would re-measure master. Run it on a check when checks reset, or add its GATE timing as a log-only probe (cap forced to 0) to the next prefill check, which costs nothing.
justification: Profile bff8e36788a04917 matches the hypothesis. On sliding turn_1, FA3 is 25.3 us and FlashAttnFwdCombine is 6.9 us, on a 747.09 us shape. Full turn_1 is 417.5 + 6.9 us. Sliding turn_4 has 61.8 us of FA3 with no combine row in its top kernels. The mechanism is that num_splits > 0 caps FA3's varlen dynamic split, which LESSONS (Attention) confirms. Cap 1 makes FA3 skip the split and the combine launch. This is the only real lever: caps 2 and 4 cannot raise the split above the heuristic, so any cap at or above FA3's chosen split is a no-op. The real candidate set is therefore {heuristic, 1}, maybe plus 2 if the heuristic picked more than 2. Full turn_1 is compute-bound at about 590 TFLOP/s (753 x 16 heads x 80K keys x 64 x 4 flops / 417.5 us), matching LESSONS' ~600 TFLOP/s ceiling, so cap 1 there can only lose. The gate will keep 0, as the spec expects. Turn_4 and first_turn being flat is consistent. Stake: 6-10 us x weight 46 = 276-460 us on a turn_1 load of about 52.5 ms (46 x 747 + 16 x 1137). That is 0.5-0.9% of one load and +0.17-0.29% on the 3-load geomean, roughly 5-10x below the CI half-width of master's score (1.426-1.470). WEAKEST LINK: whether cap 1 beats 32.2 us at all. With no split, about 64 PackGQA m-block CTAs sit on 132 SMs and each walks the whole ~17-tile band serially. If the heuristic split was 2, per-CTA work roughly doubles, while the 6.9 us combine is mostly fixed launch and tail cost. If FA3's prologue and epilogue are about 8-10 us, the unsplit kernel lands near 33-40 us, which is a wash or a loss, and the 0.97 gate correctly keeps 0. I put a cap-1 selection at about 35-40%. It is a coin flip whether the run executes anything different from master.
confounders: sglang-pipeline-parity: it defined this exact FA3 call (scheduler_metadata None on prefill, so FA3 uses the dynamic varlen split). The change depends on that path but is not confounded by it; it is the base this cap acts on.

No other landed hypothesis (stack-tonight-five, the rega s4 ports, align-two-phase, the Triton/Marlin expert stages) touches attention or runs concurrently with FA3. The router side stream forks after the o GEMM, so FA3 and the combine run alone on the GPU. Neither a gain nor a loss on the FA3 and combine rows could come from an interaction.

Not landed, but the same call site: fa3-full-contiguous-kv-triton-gather-gated (queued) edits this flash_attn_with_kvcache call on full layers. The two are shape-disjoint in intent (turn_1 full stays paged there), but they need a hand restack if both land, as the spec already says.
interference: No companion is warranted. Attribution is direct, not inferred from the headline. The '[fa3 splits] GATE' line prints the per-cap timings and the chosen cap for each class, and the turn_1 profile rows (FA3 main kernel plus whether FlashAttnFwdCombine is still present) show the effect in place. Neither a gain nor a loss is ambiguous at the kernel level. At the headline, any reading is ambiguous whatever companion you add, because the effect is far below the CI. A second scored run would buy nothing. That ambiguity is the argument against a scored run in the first place, not for a companion. If the gate logs cap 0 for every class, the run has measured master again and should be filed neutral with the GATE line as the finding (the combine is worth keeping at turn_1).
rules_flags: None blocking. num_splits comes from a prepare-time dict keyed on config (window, batch, q_len, page-table-width bucket). It is a Python int: graph-safe, with no host sync and no branching on values. Precision, every-key attention, FP8 KV and causal/window are unchanged.

Prepare-time timing runs on synthetic caches, not judge inputs, so nothing derived from inputs is cached. Keep it that way: the gate must never time or key on data['page_table'] contents, only on its shape.

Two-state prepare: the judge prepares two state copies, so the gate may run twice and could pick different caps per state. Both choices are valid, but log each one. Sharing the dict through a module global instead of the state would break the per-state rule.

Prepare budget: 4 classes x up to 4 caps x 25+ replays, plus 2x-L2 flushes. Full turn_4 is about 1.6 ms per replay, so roughly a second in total, far under 300 s even with the existing load_inline builds. Still, wrap the gate in the any-exception-means-cap-0 guard as specified.
The tests are unknown keys and use cap 0 (master), so test coverage of a non-zero cap comes only from the gate's own self-check against cap 0. That self-check is adequate for a one-int change.
open_questions: Is spending the scored submit on this worth it, or on a rega/experts hypothesis (rega_kernel is 32-36% of every turn shape)? If the slot can go elsewhere, this belongs on a check, or as a log-only probe inside another prefill check: print the GATE timings but force cap 0, so the other run's attribution is untouched.

What split did FA3's heuristic pick on sliding turn_1 (2, or more)? If it is 2, caps 2 and 4 are no-ops and the only candidate is cap 1. Print FA3's chosen split (the dynamic split count is readable in prepare from the synthetic capture) alongside the GATE line.

FINDINGS lists sliding turn_1 at 704.4 us while the bff8e profile table shows 747.09 us, two readings of the same master. The spec uses 747.1. That does not change the conclusion, but it shows run-to-run noise on this shape is about 40 us, several times the 6-10 us target, which reinforces reading the kernel rows rather than the shape total.
Does FA3's prepare_varlen_num_blocks / scheduler kernel still launch at cap 1? If it does, the saving is the combine plus the fp32 partial round trip only, and the prepare kernel's few us remain.
